ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a central carbon labeled “CCl2”, indicating that the carbon is already connected to two chlorine atoms; below the carbon there is also a “Cl” connected through a vertical line; above there is a circled negative sign, indicating that this structure carries a negative charge. The figure also draws curved arrows, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason: After ignoring the arrows, the structure can be understood as a negatively charged carbon center connected to three chlorine atoms, namely a trichloromethyl anion form. In SMILES, a negatively charged carbon needs to be written in square brackets as [C-], and the three chlorines are arranged as connected atoms/substituents, which can be written as Cl[C-](Cl)Cl.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a carbon center written as CCl2, with another Cl bonded below and a minus charge symbol above; curved arrows are present but should be ignored. Interpret the skeletal connectivity as one carbon bonded to three chlorine atoms with a negative formal charge on carbon. Convert that structure into SMILES by placing the charged carbon in brackets and listing the three Cl substituents: Cl[C-](Cl)Cl.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有一个中心碳标为“CCl2”，表示碳已经连接两个氯原子；碳的下方还有一个通过竖线相连的“Cl”；上方有一个圈出的负号，表示该结构带负电荷。图中还画有弯曲箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。
再推理：忽略箭头后，结构可理解为一个带负电荷的碳中心与三个氯原子相连，即三氯甲基负离子形式。在 SMILES 中，带负电荷的碳需要写在方括号中为[C-]，三个氯作为连接原子/取代基排列，可写作 Cl[C-](Cl)Cl。
